scan.name: wisscreen
scan.description: WICLOUD is a Next.js 16 (App Router) marketing site and platform for an IT solutions agency: a long-form marketing homepage with per-solution landing pages, plus a back-office platform (/dashboard, /admin) built on Neon Postgres, Better Auth, and Drizzle ORM. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.summary: Updates a target account's name/phone/company/admin note/magic-link flag, requiring users:write.

nodes.name: changeRole
nodes.summary: Changes a user's role, requiring team:write, refusing self-demotion and demoting the last active admin, and notifying the target of the change.

nodes.name: updatePermissions
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a user's permission overrides from a fully-posted checkbox matrix: only deviations from the target role's defaults are stored, so a later role promotion isn't overruled by a frozen snapshot.

nodes.name: setQuota
nodes.summary: Upserts a quota row (limit/used) for a user, requiring subscriptions:write, resetting the period only for non-standing metrics.

nodes.name: deleteQuota
nodes.summary: Removes a metric row from a user's quotas, which per the quota rules makes that metric unlimited again.

nodes.name: messageUser
nodes.summary: Sends an in-app notification to a target user and optionally an e-mail, requiring notifications:write.

nodes.name: impersonate
nodes.summary: Starts a Better Auth impersonation session for the target user and redirects the staff member to /dashboard, refusing self-impersonation.

nodes.name: deleteUser
nodes.summary: Permanently deletes a user account after the admin types the exact e-mail as confirmation, refusing self-deletion and deletion of the last active admin.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Back-office 'create account' page (/admin/utilisateurs/nouveau): pre-fills name/e-mail from a contact-lead query string, filters the offered role list to what the caller may actually create (team:write gates staff/admin), and warns when e-mail isn't configured.

nodes.name: NouvelUtilisateurPage
nodes.summary: Requires users:write, reads optional nom/email search params to prefill the form, computes canCreateStaff via team:write, and renders CreateUserForm with a role list filtered (not just disabled) to what the action will actually accept.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Admin user list (/admin/utilisateurs): searchable/filterable (role, active/suspended, free-text over name/e-mail/company) table of up to 300 accounts joined to their current plan, each row linking to the account's fiche.

nodes.name: UtilisateursPage
nodes.summary: Requires users:read, builds a Drizzle filter set from role/etat/q search params, joins users to their active subscription's plan name, and renders the FilterBar plus the resulting account list.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Client 'My services' page (/dashboard/abonnement): live and past subscriptions with pricing/spec/access-notes, metered-usage quota meters, and the service catalogue grouped by category with an 'owned' badge — ordering is a human step, every 'Order' opens a demande rather than checking out directly.

nodes.name: MesServicesPage
nodes.summary: Loads the client's subscriptions, quota usage and the active plan catalogue in parallel, splits subscriptions into live/past, groups the catalogue by category, and renders service cards, usage meters and orderable catalogue cards linking into the demande flow.

nodes.name: actions.ts
nodes.summary: Client-side server actions for the request (demande) thread: create a request with a retry-on-collision reference allocator, reply in the thread, mark the thread read, and self-close a request — each notifying staff and, where relevant, e-mailing the admin address.

nodes.name: insertWithRef
nodes.summary: Allocates the next WC-YYMM-NNNN reference and inserts a request, retrying up to three times on a unique-index collision from two concurrent submissions computing the same sequence number.

nodes.name: createRequest
nodes.summary: Validates and inserts a new client request (unmetered — filing a demande is never rationed), logs the activity, notifies staff with requests:read and e-mails the admin address, then redirects to the new request's page.

nodes.name: replyToRequest
nodes.summary: Appends a message to a request thread the caller owns (ownership enforced in the WHERE clause), refusing closed requests, then notifies the assignee or the whole desk and e-mails the admin.

nodes.name: markThreadRead
nodes.summary: Marks unread staff-authored messages on the caller's own request as read and publishes a realtime nudge to the assignee (or the whole requests:read desk) so their 'read' indicator updates live.

nodes.name: closeOwnRequest
nodes.summary: The client's own 'mark as done' transition — the only status change a client can make directly — logging the activity and notifying staff.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: New-request form page (/dashboard/demandes/nouvelle): pre-fills type/solution/title from query params and renders the NewRequestForm alongside a static 'what happens next' explainer panel.

nodes.name: NouvelleDemandePage
nodes.summary: Requires an authenticated user, reads solution/type/title search params, and renders NewRequestForm with type and solution options plus defaults.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Client request list (/dashboard/demandes): every request the caller has filed, rendered as a linked list (not a table, to stay readable on a phone) with status chip, type, related solution and relative timestamp.

nodes.name: DemandesPage
nodes.summary: Builds a slug-to-name map of solutions, requires an authenticated user, loads their requests via listRequests, and renders them as a list or an empty state with a CTA into the new-request flow.

nodes.name: actions.ts
nodes.summary: Customer-side server actions for the 'upload' demo block: start a processing run (re-checking entitlement and spending the demo.processing quota, currently unlimited since no service grants it) and submit an in-progress run once files are attached, notifying the desk.

nodes.name: startDemoRun
nodes.summary: Re-derives demo entitlement, reuses an already-open run instead of creating a duplicate, spends the demo.processing quota (recording a 'quota' outcome on refusal), and inserts a new pending run on success.

nodes.name: submitDemoRun
nodes.summary: Transitions a pending run with at least one uploaded attachment to 'en_cours' and notifies staff with demos:read that a file is ready to process.

nodes.name: actions.ts
nodes.summary: Client's accept/refuse decision on a quote (devis): a single UPDATE whose WHERE clause enforces both ownership and that the quote is still in 'envoye' status (so a replayed form post after withdrawal is a no-op), followed by staff notification and an admin e-mail.

nodes.name: respondToQuote
nodes.summary: Updates a quote's status to accepte/refuse guarded by ownership and current status, logs the decision, notifies staff with quotes:read and e-mails the admin, returning a decision-specific confirmation message.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Client documents page (/dashboard/documents): every file exchanged across all of the client's requests in one list, with download links, a storage-quota meter, and a FileUpload panel disabled with an explanation when object storage isn't configured.

nodes.name: DocumentsPage
nodes.summary: Requires an authenticated user, loads all owned documents and quotas in parallel, finds the storage.mb quota, sums used bytes, and renders the document list, upload panel and storage summary.

nodes.name: MarkAllReadButton.tsx
nodes.summary: Two small client buttons for the notification feed: 'mark all read' (a plain form-action submit) and 'clear read' (behind ConfirmButton's two-step arm/confirm control, since clearing deletes rows).

nodes.name: MarkAllReadButton
nodes.summary: Renders a form bound to the markAllRead server action with a submit button.

nodes.name: ClearReadButton
nodes.summary: Renders ConfirmButton wired to the clearRead server action, with a count-aware confirm label and a warning that unread notifications are kept.

nodes.name: actions.ts
nodes.summary: Server actions for a client's own notification feed (mark-all-read, mark-one-read, delete-one, clear-read): every statement is scoped to the caller by its WHERE, so there is no permission key involved, only ownership; each ends by publishing a realtime nudge and revalidating both shell layouts.

nodes.name: markAllRead
nodes.summary: Marks every unread notification belonging to the caller as read.

nodes.name: markRead
nodes.summary: Marks a single notification owned by the caller as read.

nodes.name: deleteNotification
nodes.summary: Deletes a single notification owned by the caller.

nodes.name: clearRead
nodes.summary: Deletes every already-read notification for the caller, leaving unread ones untouched.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Client notification feed page (/dashboard/notifications): the last 100 notifications for the signed-in user with an unread count in the page description.

nodes.name: NotificationsPage
nodes.summary: Requires an authenticated user, loads their last 100 notifications, and renders them through NotificationFeed.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Client dashboard home (/dashboard): a 'to-do first' layout — pending quotes and unpaid invoices at the top (the one thing blocking the agency's own work), stat tiles, recent requests, live services with hot-usage quota meters, entitled demos with expiry countdowns, and recent notifications.

nodes.name: DashboardHome
nodes.summary: Loads counters, recent requests, subscriptions, quota usage, entitled demos, recent notifications, pending quotes and overdue-or-sent invoices in parallel, computes per-document TTC via effectiveCompany/withVat, and renders the prioritized dashboard layout.

nodes.name: actions.ts
nodes.summary: Client profile server action: updates identity fields only (name/phone/company). E-mail is deliberately not editable here — changing it is an authentication change that needs Better Auth's changeEmail verification flow, not yet wired up.

nodes.name: updateProfile
nodes.summary: Validates and writes name/phone/company for the current user, logs the activity, and revalidates both the dashboard and admin layouts (since staff edit their profile from inside /admin too).

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Client profile page (/dashboard/profil): identity, password (only offered if a credential account exists — a Google-only account has none), connected-sessions list, and account deletion, plus a read-only account summary panel.

nodes.name: ProfilPage
nodes.summary: Requires an authenticated user, checks for a credential account, and renders the identity/password/session/delete panels alongside a role/verification/membership summary.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: The 403 landing page (/acces-refuse) that requirePermission() redirects a signed-in-but-unauthorized staff member to, naming the missing permission in plain French (e.g. 'Factures → Modifier') so it's actionable, with links back into /admin or /dashboard.

nodes.name: AccesRefusePage
nodes.summary: Parses the ?perm= query param into a domain:action pair, looks up human-readable labels from DOMAIN_LABELS/ACTION_LABELS, and renders the access-denied message with links back to admin or the client dashboard.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: POST /api/contact — the public contact-form endpoint: verifies Cloudflare Turnstile (skipped if unconfigured, never breaking the form outright), stores the submission as a contact_leads row (previously it verified and silently dropped the message), notifies staff with leads:read, and e-mails the admin as a convenience copy.

nodes.name: verifyTurnstile
nodes.summary: POSTs the Turnstile response token to Cloudflare's siteverify endpoint with an 8s timeout, returning true when TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY is unset (feature disabled rather than blocking every submission) and false on any error or non-success response.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Parses and validates the contact form, verifies Turnstile, inserts a contact_leads row, notifies staff, and e-mails the admin — the database write, not the e-mail, is the record of truth so a down mail provider never turns a stored lead into a visible error.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: POST /api/demos/secret — reveals one demo secret (test password, SSH key) to an entitled customer or demos:read staff and logs the reveal. A route rather than a server action because it returns a value to already-hydrated JS and needs Cache-Control: no-store; every condition (session, ban, entitlement, expiry, that the block still declares the secret) is re-checked from scratch rather than trusting the page that rendered the button.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Authenticates the caller, requires ENCRYPTION_KEY to be configured, re-derives entitlement (staff with demos:read bypass it), confirms the block still declares the requested secret and isn't expired, decrypts the ciphertext with the demo/block/label AAD, increments the reveal counter, logs the reveal, and returns the plaintext with no-store headers — refusals are 404s rather than 403s so the existence of a named secret is never leaked.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route that streams a generated PDF (devis or facture) for a given document id, enforcing ownership or the billing:read permission before rendering it with renderBillingPdf.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route that marks a single notification as read for the current user and redirects to its target href, used when a user clicks a notification link.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route returning the current user's unread notification count and a page of recent notifications, polled by the dashboard notification bell.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Server-Sent Events endpoint that streams live realtime events (unread count, notifications) to the signed-in user's browser tab, backed by Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY via lib/realtime.ts.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route handling the full upload lifecycle: presigning S3-style PUT URLs, recording finished uploads as attachments after authorizing the target (request, message, demo, demo run, company, or site), and presigning downloads with per-target access checks.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Public route that streams a public image/video attachment from the private object storage bucket by its database id, passing through Range headers for video seeking and caching for a year.

nodes.name: FilterBar.tsx
nodes.summary: Client component rendering a debounced search box plus dropdown filters that write their state into the URL's search params, used across admin list pages.

nodes.name: NotificationFeed.tsx
nodes.summary: Renders a list of notification rows (read/unread styling, relative timestamps, mark-all-read/clear actions) shared by the dashboard and admin notification pages.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Resolves the requested billing document (devis/facture) by kind and id, checks the caller owns it or holds billing:read, then streams the rendered PDF inline or as a download based on the dl query param.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Marks the given notification id as read (scoped to the current user), publishes the updated unread state over realtime, then redirects to the notification's in-app href or to the dashboard root if the target isn't a safe in-app path.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Fetches the current user's unread count and recent notifications in parallel and returns them as JSON with ISO-formatted timestamps.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Opens a ReadableStream SSE connection for the current user: sends the initial unread count, subscribes to realtime events via subscribe(), heartbeats every 25s, and tears the stream down after 30 minutes or on client disconnect.

nodes.name: resolveTarget
nodes.summary: Resolves and authorizes which entity (request, message, demo, demo run, company settings, or site content) an upload/download should attach to, checking staff permissions or demo entitlement for each target kind.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Presign step: validates the upload request body, checks the content type is allowed, resolves and authorizes the target, then returns a presigned S3 PUT URL and object key.

nodes.name: PUT
nodes.summary: Finalize step: after the browser has uploaded directly to storage, validates the key belongs to the current user, re-authorizes the target, consumes storage quota, records the attachments row, and logs the activity.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Looks up an attachment by id, checks the caller may download it, then redirects to a freshly presigned download URL.

nodes.name: mayDownload
nodes.summary: Authorization check for reading an attachment: allows the uploader, staff with the right permission, or a customer entitled to the demo it belongs to.

nodes.name: mayAttachTo
nodes.summary: Authorization check for attaching an upload to a support request: allows staff with requests:write or the request's own owner.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Looks up a public attachment's storage key and content type, streams the bytes from object storage with Range support, and sets long-lived cache headers since ids are immutable.

nodes.name: FilterBar
nodes.summary: Renders a search input (debounced via a client-side timeout) and a row of select filters, pushing changes to the URL query string with useTransition so list pages re-render from server data.

nodes.name: NotificationFeed
nodes.summary: Renders notification rows with unread styling and relative timestamps, an empty state, and the mark-all-read / clear-read action buttons above the list.

nodes.name: PageHeader.tsx
nodes.summary: Shared dashboard/admin layout primitives: a page title/back-link header, a bordered content Panel, and a StatTile metric card, used to keep list and detail pages visually consistent.

nodes.name: ProfileForms.tsx
nodes.summary: Client forms for the shared 'Mon profil' page (used by both dashboard and admin shells): identity fields, password change, active session list with revoke, and account deletion.

nodes.name: QuotaMeter.tsx
nodes.summary: Renders a single quota's usage as a labeled progress bar (percentage, used/limit, optional reset date), color-coded as it approaches its limit.

nodes.name: pills.ts
nodes.summary: Shared Tailwind class-string constants for pill/badge styling (primary, outline, soft, and a small-size modifier) reused across dashboard status chips and tags.

nodes.name: account.ts
nodes.summary: Account-side side effects shared across server actions: activity-log entries, creating and realtime-publishing notifications (single or bulk), resolving which staff hold a given permission, and reading unread/recent notifications for a user.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Lazily-constructed Drizzle/node-postgres database client, exposed as `db` through a Proxy so importing this module never opens a connection until a query actually runs — required so CI/CD builds with no DATABASE_URL still succeed.

nodes.name: schema.ts
nodes.summary: The application's full Drizzle ORM schema: Better Auth tables (user/session/account/verification), billing (plans, subscriptions, quotas, quotes, invoices), support requests and messages, attachments, demos and their access/secrets/runs, notifications, activity log, app settings, contact leads, and the owner-editable site content/solutions tables.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-file Drizzle schema definition with 22 exported tables; no functions, just table/column declarations and relations.

nodes.name: seed.ts
nodes.summary: One-off seed script (run by hand, never at app start) that upserts the service catalogue's plans, deactivates ones no longer offered, cancels the legacy free 'Découverte' subscriptions, and fills in any missing default app settings without overwriting admin-edited ones.

nodes.name: PageHeader
nodes.summary: Renders the page's title (auto-punctuated), optional description, an optional back link, and an actions slot at the top of a dashboard/admin page.

nodes.name: Panel
nodes.summary: A bordered card wrapper with an optional header (title/description/actions) used to group dashboard content sections.

nodes.name: StatTile
nodes.summary: A single metric tile showing a label, value, optional hint and icon, optionally rendered as a link, with a cool or signal color tone.

nodes.name: IdentityForm
nodes.summary: Server-action-backed form for editing name, phone and company on the account, using useActionState for pending/error state.

nodes.name: PasswordForm
nodes.summary: Form for changing the account password via authClient.changePassword, validating the new/confirm fields match before submitting and resetting on success.

nodes.name: SessionList
nodes.summary: Fetches and lists the account's active sessions with a parsed user-agent description and last-active time, letting the user revoke a single session or all others.

nodes.name: describeAgent
nodes.summary: Parses a raw User-Agent string into a short human-readable browser + OS label (e.g. 'Chrome sur Windows') for the session list.

nodes.name: DeleteAccount
nodes.summary: Two-step, password-confirmed account deletion control: an arming click reveals a password field, and confirming calls authClient.deleteUser before redirecting home.

nodes.name: QuotaMeter
nodes.summary: Renders a quota row: label, used/limit or 'illimité', a progress bar that shifts color near capacity, and an optional reset date.

nodes.name: logActivity
nodes.summary: Inserts one row into the activity log (actor, action, target, metadata), swallowing failures so a broken audit write never blocks the action it's logging.

nodes.name: kindFor
nodes.summary: Maps a notification's semantic type (e.g. request reply, quote sent) to the coarse UI kind used to pick its icon/color.

nodes.name: row
nodes.summary: Builds the row shape inserted into the notifications table for a given user id and notification entry.

nodes.name: notify
nodes.summary: Inserts a notification for one user and publishes it over realtime so any open tab updates immediately.

nodes.name: notifyMany
nodes.summary: Inserts the same notification for a deduplicated list of user ids and publishes it to all of them over realtime in one batch.

nodes.name: staffWith
nodes.summary: Finds active, non-banned staff/admin accounts that currently hold a given permission (via role default or explicit grant), optionally excluding one user — used to target who gets notified.

nodes.name: notifyStaff
nodes.summary: Notifies every staff member holding a given permission (except an optional excluded user) with the same notification entry.

nodes.name: unreadCount
nodes.summary: Counts a user's unread notifications.

nodes.name: recentNotifications
nodes.summary: Returns a user's most recent notifications, newest first, up to a limit.

nodes.name: getPool
nodes.summary: Builds the pg.Pool from DATABASE_URL (or DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED) on first use, throwing if neither env var is set.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs the seed: upserts each plan row, deactivates stale plan slugs, cancels legacy Découverte subscriptions, and inserts default app settings only where none exist yet, then exits.

nodes.name: email.ts
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around the Resend API for transactional email: degrades to console-logging the message (including any verification/reset links) when RESEND_API_KEY is unset, so the whole sign-up flow stays completable with no mailbox.

nodes.name: format.ts
nodes.summary: Small collection of locale-aware date, relative-time and byte-size formatting helpers (Africa/Algiers timezone, fr-FR locale) shared across the dashboard and admin UI.

nodes.name: guard.ts
nodes.summary: Server-side auth guards used by every dashboard/admin page and server action: reading the current session/user, requiring sign-in or staff role, requiring a specific permission (with a named redirect), and asserting ownership-or-permission for a resource.

nodes.name: kv.ts
nodes.summary: Parsing/formatting helpers for the simple 'key: value' text-area format used by a few admin forms (free-form specs and quota grants), including validation of quota grant syntax.

nodes.name: permissions.ts
nodes.summary: The authorization core: role/permission domain definitions and admin-UI labels, plus can()/isStaff()/effectivePermissions(), which resolve a permission by layering an account's explicit permissions jsonb over its role's defaults.

nodes.name: quotas.ts
nodes.summary: Consumable-quota engine: granting/revoking a plan's quota metrics to a user, atomically consuming and refunding usage with lazy period resets, and listing a user's quotas and provisioned subscriptions.

nodes.name: realtime.ts
nodes.summary: Server-Sent-Events backbone built on Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY: publish()/publishMany() NOTIFY a per-user channel after a DB write, and subscribe() (used by the SSE route) registers a callback and lazily owns one dedicated, auto-reconnecting LISTEN client on the unpooled connection.

nodes.name: requests.ts
nodes.summary: Domain constants and helpers for support requests: status/type/priority enums and their French labels, the allowed status transition graph, and status-badge color tones.

nodes.name: emailConfigured
nodes.summary: Reports whether a Resend API key is configured.

nodes.name: adminEmail
nodes.summary: Reads the configured admin notification email address from the environment.

nodes.name: sendEmail
nodes.summary: Sends an email via Resend (subject, wrapped HTML body, optional attachments and reply-to); if no API key is set, logs the message and its links to the console instead of sending.

nodes.name: wrap
nodes.summary: Wraps a plain-text message body in the shared branded HTML email template, splitting paragraphs and optionally adding a call-to-action button.

nodes.name: formatDate
nodes.summary: Formats a date as a short French date string.

nodes.name: formatDateTime
nodes.summary: Formats a date as a French date+time string.

nodes.name: toDateInput
nodes.summary: Formats a date as an ISO yyyy-mm-dd string suitable for an <input type=date> value.

nodes.name: relativeTime
nodes.summary: Formats a date as a relative French phrase (e.g. 'il y a 3 jours') using Intl.RelativeTimeFormat, picking the coarsest unit that fits.

nodes.name: formatBytes
nodes.summary: Formats a byte count as a human-readable size string (o/Ko/Mo/Go).

nodes.name: daysAgo
nodes.summary: Returns a Date offset a given number of days before now, used for building relative-time test/demo data.

nodes.name: getCurrentSession
nodes.summary: Reads the current Better Auth session from the request headers.

nodes.name: getCurrentUser
nodes.summary: Returns the current session's user, or null if signed out.

nodes.name: isImpersonating
nodes.summary: Reports whether the current session is a staff member impersonating another user.

nodes.name: requireUser
nodes.summary: Redirects to /connexion (preserving a return path) if there's no signed-in user, otherwise returns them; used at the top of every protected page.

nodes.name: requireStaff
nodes.summary: Requires a signed-in user and redirects home if they aren't staff or admin.

nodes.name: requirePermission
nodes.summary: Requires a signed-in user holding a specific permission key, redirecting to /acces-refuse naming the missing permission otherwise.

nodes.name: assertOwnerOrPermission
nodes.summary: Guards a resource-detail page: returns normally if the current user owns the resource or holds the given permission, otherwise triggers a Next.js notFound() rather than revealing the resource exists.

nodes.name: allowed
nodes.summary: Boolean permission check for a possibly-null principal, used in server components/actions that need a plain yes/no instead of a redirect.

nodes.name: parseLines
nodes.summary: Parses 'key: value' lines from a textarea into an ordered array of [key, value] pairs, ignoring blank lines and lines without a colon.

nodes.name: formatLines
nodes.summary: Formats a metric->limit map back into 'key: value' lines, rendering a null limit as 'illimité'.

nodes.name: parseGrants
nodes.summary: Parses and validates a 'metric: limit' textarea into a metric->limit map, accepting 'illimité'/'unlimited'/'∞' as null and rejecting malformed keys or non-integer limits.

nodes.name: listLines
nodes.summary: Parses a free-text list (one item per line, optional bullet marker) into a trimmed, non-empty array of strings.

nodes.name: can
nodes.summary: Answers whether a principal (user row or role string) has a given permission key: an explicit true/false override in the account's permissions jsonb wins, otherwise falls back to the role's default set.

nodes.name: isStaff
nodes.summary: Reports whether a principal holds any permission at all beyond the plain 'user' defaults — the practical definition of 'is staff'.

nodes.name: effectivePermissions
nodes.summary: Computes the full resolved permission map (every key -> boolean) for a principal, used to render the admin permissions editor.

nodes.name: isRoleDefault
nodes.summary: Reports whether a permission key is part of a given role's default set, used to show which admin-UI checkboxes are role-inherited vs explicitly overridden.

nodes.name: nextPeriodReset
nodes.summary: Computes the UTC timestamp for the first of next month, used as a quota's next reset date.

nodes.name: describe
nodes.summary: Turns a raw quota row into a display-ready shape: percentage used, remaining, and whether it's unlimited/exhausted.

nodes.name: listQuotas
nodes.summary: Lists a user's quotas, described and sorted by label.

nodes.name: grantServiceQuotas
nodes.summary: Upserts (adds to, never replaces) a set of metric grants for a user when a service is provisioned, using a standing (never-expiring) reset for metrics like storage and a monthly reset for consumable ones.

nodes.name: revokeServiceQuotas
nodes.summary: Reduces a user's quota limits by a service's grants when it's cancelled, floored at zero.

nodes.name: consume
nodes.summary: Atomically increments a quota's usage in one UPDATE ... WHERE that also enforces the limit, so two concurrent requests can never both succeed past capacity; lazily resets an expired period in the same statement. Returns ok/unlimited/exceeded.

nodes.name: refund
nodes.summary: Decrements a quota's usage (e.g. after a failed operation), floored at zero.

nodes.name: listSubscriptions
nodes.summary: Lists a user's provisioned services (subscriptions joined with their plan), newest first.

nodes.name: channelFor
nodes.summary: Derives a Postgres NOTIFY channel name from a user id.

nodes.name: publish
nodes.summary: NOTIFYs a single user's realtime channel with a JSON-encoded event, through the pooled connection (fine for NOTIFY, unlike LISTEN).

nodes.name: publishMany
nodes.summary: NOTIFYs several users' channels with the same event in one batched SQL statement.

nodes.name: ensureClient
nodes.summary: Lazily opens (or reuses) the dedicated pg.Client used for LISTEN, on the unpooled DATABASE_URL — required because Neon's pooled endpoint hands connections back between statements and a LISTEN there never receives anything. Wires notification/error/end handlers, with reconnect-with-backoff on drop.

nodes.name: resubscribeAll
nodes.summary: Re-issues LISTEN for every channel with active subscribers, used after the LISTEN client reconnects following a dropped connection.

nodes.name: subscribe
nodes.summary: Registers a callback for a user's realtime events, issuing LISTEN on first subscriber and UNLISTEN when the last one for that user unsubscribes; returns an unsubscribe function.

nodes.name: canTransition
nodes.summary: Checks whether a request status transition is legal per the fixed TRANSITIONS graph.

nodes.name: isRequestStatus
nodes.summary: Type guard checking a string is one of the valid request statuses.

nodes.name: isClosed
nodes.summary: Reports whether a request status is a terminal (closed) one.

nodes.name: document-overrides.test.tsx

nodes.name: pdf.test.tsx

nodes.name: platform.test.ts

nodes.summary: Client form for creating or editing a sellable service-catalogue item (name, category, price, specs, quota grants), plus a type-to-confirm delete form that keeps already-sold subscriptions intact when an offer is removed.

nodes.summary: The four desk-side controls on a client request: change status (only to states nextStatuses() permits), assign an owner and priority, edit the client's own title/description/budget, and a type-to-confirm delete — deliberately four separate forms so each server action logs a distinct, unambiguous change.

nodes.name: ServiceForm

nodes.name: DeleteCatalogueForm
nodes.summary: Type-to-confirm delete of a catalogue offer; existing subscriptions sold from it keep their own price and specs and only lose the link back to the offer.

nodes.summary: Toggleable inline form correcting the client's own title, description and budget — an internal correction that does not notify the client.

nodes.summary: Type-to-confirm delete of a request, its thread and attachments; linked quotes/services survive without the back-reference.

nodes.name: QuoteActions
nodes.summary: Renders only the actions valid for a quote's current status: PDF links, send/resend by e-mail, convert an accepted quote to an invoice or link to provisioning, and a confirm delete gated by the reference once the client has already been sent the document.

nodes.name: AdminQuotePage
nodes.summary: Loads a quote with its client, resolves the effective per-document company identity, and renders the live editor while the quote is still answerable or a frozen read-only preview once the client has responded, plus client/status/linked-document panels.

nodes.name: actions.ts
nodes.summary: Server actions for the lifecycle of a quote (devis): save (draft create/update, refuses edits once the client has answered), send/resend by e-mail with PDF attached and client notification, convert an accepted quote into an invoice by copying its lines, and delete (plain confirm for drafts, reference-typed confirm once sent).

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: New-quote admin page: checks quotes:write, loads billable clients and the company identity, optionally prefilling from a linked request id in the query string, and renders the DocumentEditor for a blank devis.

nodes.name: InvoiceActions.tsx

nodes.name: InvoiceControls.tsx
nodes.summary: Small inline form to move an invoice through its statuses (mainly marking it paid) and adjust its due date, since there is no payment provider and a human sets invoice state by hand.

nodes.name: page.tsx

nodes.name: actions.ts
nodes.summary: Server actions for the invoice lifecycle: save (create/update, refuses paid/cancelled invoices), send/resend by e-mail (issues on first send, stamps issuedAt), status transitions (stamps issuedAt/paidAt on the transition rather than recomputing, notifies the client when marked paid), and delete (plain confirm for drafts, reference-typed confirm once emitted).

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: New-invoice admin page: checks invoices:write, loads billable clients and the company identity, and renders the DocumentEditor for a blank facture.

nodes.name: PurgeForm.tsx
nodes.summary: Confirm-gated form that purges activity-log entries older than a chosen date; the purge action itself stays recorded in the journal.

nodes.name: saveQuote
nodes.summary: Creates or updates a quote draft; refuses to edit a quote the client has already answered since it is a document of record, and allocates the DV- reference only on creation.

nodes.name: sendQuote
nodes.summary: E-mails the quote's PDF; from a draft this is the first time the client can see it (moves status to envoye and notifies), from any later state it is a plain resend with no status change.

nodes.name: invoiceFromQuote
nodes.summary: Turns an accepted quote into an invoice by copying its lines and overrides (never referencing them, so a later quote correction cannot retroactively change what was billed); redirects to an existing invoice if one was already created from this quote.

nodes.name: deleteQuote
nodes.summary: Deletes a quote; a draft needs only a plain confirm, one the client has seen requires typing the reference. An invoice already made from it survives with quoteId set to null.

nodes.name: NouveauDevisPage
nodes.summary: Loads billable clients and the company identity for a blank quote editor, optionally prefilling the linked request from a `demande` query parameter.

nodes.name: InvoiceActions
nodes.summary: PDF preview/download links, send/resend by e-mail, and a reference-gated confirm delete for an invoice.

nodes.name: InvoiceControls
nodes.summary: Inline status/due-date form driving setInvoiceStatus — the manual substitute for a payment provider.

nodes.name: AdminInvoicePage
nodes.summary: Loads an invoice with its client and originating quote, resolves the effective per-document company identity, and renders the live editor or a frozen read-only preview depending on invoice status, plus client/status/action panels.

nodes.name: saveInvoice
nodes.summary: Creates or updates an invoice draft; a paid or cancelled invoice is a closed accounting record and cannot be edited (an avoir or new invoice is the way out).

nodes.name: insertWithRef
nodes.summary: Allocates an FA-YYMM-NNNN reference and inserts the invoice, retrying up to twice on the reference's unique-index collision.

nodes.name: sendInvoice
nodes.summary: E-mails the invoice's PDF; from a draft this also issues it (status envoyee, issuedAt stamped) and notifies the client, otherwise it is a plain resend.

nodes.name: setInvoiceStatus
nodes.summary: Moves an invoice through its states by hand — the whole billing workflow given there is no payment provider — stamping issuedAt/paidAt on the transition itself and notifying the client when marked paid.

nodes.name: deleteInvoice
nodes.summary: Deletes an invoice; a draft needs only a plain confirm, one already sent requires typing the reference (cancelling is usually the better move for a paid invoice, since it keeps the record).

nodes.name: NewInvoicePage
nodes.summary: Loads billable clients and the company identity for a blank invoice editor.

nodes.name: PurgeForm
nodes.summary: Confirm-gated form purging activity-log entries older than a chosen date.

nodes.name: BroadcastForm.tsx
nodes.summary: Compose-a-broadcast form: picks a recipient segment (all active, clients only, team, recent signups, or a specific plan's customers) and shows the live recipient count computed server-side before sending a titled message with an optional e-mail copy.

nodes.name: segments.ts
nodes.summary: Shared constant list of broadcast recipient segments (tous, clients, équipe, nouveaux, plan) and their value union, pulled out of the '"use server"' actions file because a server-actions module may only export async functions.

nodes.name: CompanyForm.tsx
nodes.summary: The header/footer/legal/bank identity printed on every devis and facture PDF: company name, legal IDs (RC/NIF/NIS/AI), bank details, VAT rate, logo/signature pickers, and free-text terms — every field optional so an admin can start sending quotes before the paperwork is fully collected.

nodes.name: SettingsForm.tsx
nodes.summary: Platform-wide switches form: magic-link sign-in, open registration, required e-mail verification, and the announcement banner shown across both dashboard shells.

nodes.name: actions.ts
nodes.summary: Server actions for platform settings: updateSettings writes each app_settings key individually so a switch un-ticking turns it off rather than leaving it untouched, and updateCompany validates the logo/signature are PNG or JPEG attachments (the PDF engine can't embed anything else) before saving the printed company identity.

nodes.name: UserControls.tsx
nodes.summary: Every control on the admin user detail page, one form per action: profile fields, role change, the permission-matrix editor (draft state reseeded on role change, only exceptions to the role's defaults are saved), per-metric quota grants, suspend/unsuspend, an internal message, impersonation, and a type-to-confirm irreversible account delete.

nodes.name: CreateUserForm.tsx
nodes.summary: Opens a new client or staff account from the back-office; the password field is optional and left blank triggers a generated password shown once in the success banner, which is the whole reason this page exists instead of just sending a sign-up link.

nodes.name: BroadcastForm
nodes.summary: Compose-a-broadcast form: audience segment picker (including a specific plan's customers), a live server-computed recipient count next to the send button, title/body/link, and an optional e-mail copy.

nodes.name: CompanyForm
nodes.summary: The PDF-header/footer company identity form (name, legal IDs, bank, VAT rate, logo/signature, terms); every field is optional so an admin can start billing before all paperwork is collected.

nodes.name: StatefulPicker
nodes.summary: Wraps ImagePicker with local id state so the logo/signature attachment id posts as a form field.

nodes.name: SettingsForm
nodes.summary: Platform switches form: magic-link sign-in, open registration, required e-mail verification, and the cross-dashboard announcement banner text.

nodes.name: updateSettings
nodes.summary: Writes each app_settings key individually (so app_settings stays queryable one row at a time) and revalidates every layout that shows the announcement banner or gates sign-in.

nodes.name: updateCompany
nodes.summary: Validates that any chosen logo/signature attachment exists and is PNG or JPEG (the PDF engine can't embed anything else) before saving the company identity printed on future documents.

nodes.name: UserProfileForm
nodes.summary: Edits a user's profile fields (name, phone, company, internal note) and whether magic-link sign-in is enabled for that individual account.

nodes.name: RoleForm
nodes.summary: Changes a user's role; refuses to render a submittable form for the signed-in admin's own account.

Draft state is reseeded whenever the parent remounts it on role change.

nodes.name: QuotaForm
nodes.summary: One metered quota row, or (with metric omitted) the 'add a new metric' row, letting an admin hand-grant an allowance the client's plan never created; a submit-adjacent form calls deleteQuota to remove a grant.

nodes.name: SuspendForm
nodes.summary: Two-step (armed, then confirmed) suspend control with a reason shown to the suspended person, or a one-click reactivate once banned; refuses to render for the admin's own account.

nodes.name: MessageForm
nodes.summary: Sends a titled internal-platform message to the user, optionally also by e-mail.

nodes.name: ImpersonateButton
nodes.summary: One-click 'view the platform as this user' control; hidden for the admin's own account.

nodes.name: DeleteUserForm
nodes.summary: Type-the-email-to-confirm irreversible account delete, cascading to the user's requests, messages, devis, factures, services, documents and notifications.

nodes.name: CreateUserForm
nodes.summary: Opens a client or staff account; a blank password field triggers a server-generated one shown once in the success banner, and a link to the new account's fiche appears on success.

nodes.name: NewRequestForm.tsx

nodes.name: NewRequestForm

nodes.summary: Renders the accept/refuse submit buttons for one quote and swaps to a `FormAlert` once a decision has been recorded.

nodes.name: ImagePicker.tsx
nodes.summary: Logo/signature upload control for the document editor: validates PNG/JPEG, uploads via `uploadFile`, and shows a preview with a reset option.

nodes.name: ui.tsx
nodes.summary: Shared dashboard form/UI primitives — labeled inputs, textareas, checkboxes, selects, a submit button, an action-state alert, status chips, an empty state, and a two-step destructive `ConfirmButton` — plus a re-export of HeroUI's `Button`/`Chip`.

nodes.name: billing-lines.ts

nodes.name: billing-send.ts

nodes.name: billing.ts
nodes.summary: Status vocabulary and small predicates for quotes and invoices: valid status lists, French labels and status-chip tones, quote-expiry and invoice-overdue detection.

nodes.name: company.ts
nodes.summary: The default company identity used on billing documents, the field keys that can be overridden per document, a length-capped Zod schema for those overrides, and `effectiveCompany`/`parseOverrides` to merge and validate them.

nodes.name: ImagePicker
nodes.summary: File-picker control that validates a PNG/JPEG selection, uploads it via `uploadFile`, and reports the resulting URL/attachment id to the caller, with a reset button back to the default.

nodes.name: Field
nodes.summary: Labeled single-line text input wrapping HeroUI's `TextField`, with description/error/required styling shared across dashboard forms.

nodes.name: TextAreaField
nodes.summary: Labeled multi-line textarea variant of `Field` for longer free-text inputs.

nodes.name: CheckboxField

nodes.name: SelectField
nodes.summary: Labeled dropdown wrapping HeroUI's `Select`/`ListBox`, rendering a list of `{value,label}` options.

nodes.name: SubmitButton
nodes.summary: Submit button that reads `useFormStatus` to show a pending spinner and disable itself while its form is submitting.

nodes.name: FormAlert
nodes.summary: Renders a server action's `ActionState` (success or failure message) as a styled banner.

nodes.name: StatusChip
nodes.summary: Small colored pill for a status label, toned by the caller (e.g. quote/invoice/subscription state).

nodes.name: EmptyState
nodes.summary: Generic empty-list placeholder with a title, description and optional call-to-action.

nodes.summary: Two-step destructive action button: an unarmed press reveals a confirmation panel (optionally requiring a typed confirmation phrase) before the real, red submit fires.

nodes.summary: Validates `FormData` against a Zod schema, collapsing repeated keys into arrays for multi-selects; on failure returns per-field error messages plus the raw values so the form can repopulate itself.

nodes.summary: Builds a failed `ActionState` with a message and optional field errors.

nodes.summary: Builds a successful `ActionState` with a message.

nodes.summary: Reads the parallel `label`/`quantity`/`unitCents` fields posted by the line-item form into typed `{label, quantity, unitCents}` rows, dropping blank labels.

nodes.name: readOverrides
nodes.summary: Parses the posted company-override JSON and, for any referenced logo/signature attachment ids, confirms in the database that they exist and are PNG/JPEG before accepting them.

nodes.name: toPreviewLines
nodes.summary: Converts stored cents-based billing lines into the string-valued shape the editable preview form binds to.

nodes.name: previewDoc
nodes.summary: Assembles a full preview `doc` object (dates, lines, computed total) from draft input for the live document preview.

nodes.name: emailBillingDocument
nodes.summary: Renders a quote/invoice to PDF, optionally stores it as an attachment when object storage is configured, e-mails the client with amount/date summary and an in-app link, and stamps the row as sent.

nodes.summary: True when a quote has a `validUntil` date that has passed.

nodes.summary: Type guard narrowing a string to a known `QuoteStatus`.

nodes.name: isInvoiceStatus
nodes.summary: Type guard narrowing a string to a known `InvoiceStatus`.

nodes.summary: Merges a document's per-field overrides onto the base company identity, keeping the base value wherever no override is set.

nodes.name: money.ts

nodes.name: BillingDocument.tsx

nodes.name: quota-labels.ts

nodes.name: queries.ts

nodes.name: formatMoney

nodes.name: SocialIcon

nodes.name: Turnstile
nodes.summary: Loads the Cloudflare Turnstile script, explicit-renders the widget into a container ref, and resets it whenever resetKey changes; cleans up the widget on unmount.

nodes.name: TypeCycle.tsx
nodes.summary: Typewriter-effect component that types and deletes a rotating list of words character by character behind a glowing caret, rendering the first word statically on the server to avoid layout shift for crawlers.

nodes.name: TypeCycle
nodes.summary: Drives a holding/deleting/typing state machine via chained setTimeouts to type and erase each word in the `words` list, cycling indefinitely.

nodes.name: cn.ts

nodes.name: cn
nodes.summary: Joins a variadic list of class name strings, dropping falsy entries.

nodes.summary: Client components for every auth form (sign-in, sign-up, forgot/reset password, sign-out) plus shared UI pieces (password strength field with generator, Google button, alerts); each form calls Better Auth's client directly and routes by role on success.

nodes.name: AppShell

nodes.name: ShellLink
nodes.summary: Sidebar navigation link that reflects active state and adapts its label visibility to the current sidebar mode (open/closed/hover).

nodes.name: auth-client.ts
nodes.summary: Better Auth React client instance configured with the admin and magic-link plugins, re-exporting signIn/signUp/signOut/useSession/getSession for use across auth forms and dashboard components.

nodes.name: checkPassword

nodes.name: isStrongPassword

nodes.name: generatePassword

nodes.name: isDarkTheme

nodes.name: CopyLine
nodes.summary: A labelled value with a copy-to-clipboard button and a brief 'copied' confirmation state.

nodes.name: crypto.ts
nodes.summary: AES-256-GCM encryption at rest for demo secrets (passwords, SSH keys): a versioned base64url blob format, per-value random IV, and an AAD binding each ciphertext to its owning row so a copied ciphertext fails to decrypt elsewhere.
nodes.languageNotes: Unlike every other optional integration in the project, this one does not degrade to a lesser feature when ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset — encryptSecret throws rather than ever storing a secret in plaintext.

nodes.name: encryptionConfigured
nodes.summary: Reports whether a valid 32-byte ENCRYPTION_KEY is set, by attempting to derive the key and catching failure.

nodes.name: key
nodes.summary: Reads and validates ENCRYPTION_KEY from the environment as a 32-byte base64 buffer, throwing a descriptive error (including the openssl command to generate one) if missing or the wrong length.

nodes.name: encryptSecret
nodes.summary: Encrypts a plaintext secret with AES-256-GCM under a random 12-byte IV and the caller-supplied AAD, returning a versioned `v1:iv:tag:ciphertext` base64url blob.

nodes.name: decryptSecret
nodes.summary: Decrypts a `v1:iv:tag:ciphertext` blob, verifying the auth tag against the caller-supplied AAD so a ciphertext moved to another row fails loudly instead of decrypting.

nodes.name: demoSecretAad
nodes.summary: Builds the single canonical AAD string (`demo:<demoId>:<blockId>:<label>`) shared by every writer and reader of a demo secret, so the binding can never drift between the two.

nodes.name: demos.ts

nodes.languageNotes: DemoBlockSchema is a Zod discriminated union keyed on `kind`, letting parseBlocks silently drop a stored block that no longer validates instead of failing the whole page.

nodes.name: declaredSecrets

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage Docker build for the production Next.js 16 image: installs dependencies with a frozen pnpm lockfile, builds the standalone output with the public NEXT_PUBLIC_* build args, then ships a minimal Alpine runtime that runs as a non-root user on port 3000.
nodes.languageNotes: Four stages (base/deps/builder/runner) built around Next's `output: "standalone"`, so the final image only carries traced runtime deps and server.js rather than the build toolchain or full node_modules.

nodes.name: base
nodes.summary: Base stage: node:22-alpine with libc6-compat installed (for native deps expecting glibc symbols on musl) and Corepack enabled for pnpm; every later stage builds from it.

nodes.name: deps
nodes.summary: Installs dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` from only the lockfile-affecting files (package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm-workspace.yaml), so this layer caches across source-only changes.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: Copies node_modules from deps plus the full source, injects NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY as build ARGs (Next inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars into the client bundle at build time, not at container start), and runs `pnpm build`.

nodes.name: runner
nodes.summary: Minimal runtime stage: creates an unprivileged nextjs user, copies public/ and the traced standalone server plus static assets from builder, and runs `node server.js` on port 3000.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Build-context exclusions for the Docker image: strips node_modules, build output, VCS/CI/editor files, local tooling/docs, and every .env* secret except .env.example, so none of it is baked into an image layer.

nodes.name: ci-cd.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that verifies every push and pull request against main (lint, test, build, typecheck) and, only on a push to main, builds and pushes the Docker image to Docker Hub.
nodes.languageNotes: Typecheck deliberately runs after Build because tsc depends on route types Next.js generates into .next/types during the build.

nodes.name: verify
nodes.summary: Quality-gate job that checks out the repo, installs dependencies with pnpm, then runs lint, tests, a production build, and typecheck on every push and PR.

nodes.name: docker
nodes.summary: Publish job, gated on the verify job and on pushes to main, that logs into Docker Hub, derives image tags, and builds/pushes the image with GitHub Actions layer caching and public NEXT_PUBLIC_* build args.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: AGENTS.md is the project's real README: it lays out WICLOUD as a dual-product codebase — a French-copy, GSAP/3D-heavy marketing site plus a client/admin platform on Neon Postgres and Better Auth. It documents the stack decisions (App Router, Tailwind v4, HeroUI scoped to the platform only), the strict brand palette with WCAG contrast rules, and the content model that lets the site owner edit copy from an admin panel. Read this first — every later step in this tour refers back to conventions defined here.

tour.title: Root Layout — The Real Entry Point
tour.description: app/layout.tsx is the document shell for the whole app: it builds global metadata (title, OG image, icons) from site content, loads fonts, and wraps every route. It is intentionally thin — Navbar and Footer are NOT here, because they only belong to the marketing pages, which live in their own route group. This file is what every page in the app, marketing or platform, ultimately renders inside.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router: `app/layout.tsx` is the root layout and applies to every route. Route groups like `(marketing)` and `(app)` let child folders add their own nested layout (chrome, data fetching) without changing the URL — the parenthesized segment is stripped from the path.

tour.title: Marketing Homepage Composition
tour.description: app/(marketing)/layout.tsx fetches the owner-editable site content and solutions once and wraps every marketing page with the Navbar and Footer that the root layout deliberately omitted. app/(marketing)/page.tsx is the homepage itself: an async server component that reads that content once and composes roughly twenty sections in order (Hero, HighlightsReel, PerformanceMetrics, UniverseReveal, DeviceShowcase, and more), skipping any section the owner has hidden. This is the highest fan-out file in the codebase — a good sign it's the project's true overview page.

tour.title: Two Homepage Sections in Practice
tour.description: Hero.tsx is the opening section: copy on the left, a 3D visual (globe or infrastructure stack) or media on the right, with the owner choosing both the visual mode and the width split in /admin/site. HighlightsReel is 'Section 2' — an auto-advancing carousel cycling through each solution as a stats card or a full-bleed image, gated to only autoplay while the section is actually on screen. Together they show the pattern the rest of the homepage follows: server-rendered copy, a client component for anything that needs to hydrate (animation, 3D, carousel state).
tour.languageLesson: GSAP + ScrollTrigger drive the scroll-linked reveals; the 3D scenes (`@react-three/fiber` + `drei`) are loaded via `next/dynamic` so only the chosen scene's chunk is ever fetched, and both mount only once the browser is idle so text and CTAs hydrate first.

tour.title: The Content Model — Copy and Media, Separated
tour.description: lib/data/services.ts exports SERVICES, the default copy and structure for the four solutions (OCR, Cloud Infrastructure, WIFACILITY, SETYCORE) — but it holds no media paths at all. lib/data/media.ts is the single registry of every photo, video, and external link on the site; a `withMedia()` helper copies those assets onto each service as SERVICES is built. This split means filling the site with real assets is a one-file change, and there is exactly one place to look when something renders a placeholder instead of a real image.

tour.title: The CMS Override Layer
tour.description: The defaults from Step 5 are just fallbacks — the real site content is owner-editable from /admin/site. lib/content/schema.ts defines Zod schemas for every editable field; lib/content/defaults.ts mirrors the component defaults (lifted verbatim from services.ts and the homepage sections); lib/content/index.ts is the read path that deep-merges whatever is stored in the database over those defaults and re-validates the result. Only the raw database rows are cached, not the merged object — so a newly-added field still gets its default immediately instead of serving `undefined` until a cache expires.
tour.languageLesson: Zod schemas double as runtime validators and TypeScript types — the same schema that types a form in the admin editor also re-validates whatever comes back out of the database, so a malformed stored row falls back to defaults instead of breaking the page.

tour.title: Authentication and Role-Based Routing
tour.description: lib/auth.ts is the Better Auth server instance (Drizzle Postgres adapter, email+password, optional Google sign-in) — the single source of truth for who a visitor is. proxy.ts (Next 16's renamed middleware.ts) does only an optimistic cookie check to keep anonymous traffic off dashboard renders; it decides nothing about permissions. AuthForms.tsx renders every sign-in/sign-up form and routes a signed-in user by role: staff and admin land on /admin, everyone else on /dashboard. This is the seam between the public marketing site from Steps 3-4 and the platform the rest of the tour covers.

tour.title: The Platform Shell and Authorization
tour.description: AppShell.tsx is the shared chrome for both /dashboard and /admin — a collapsible sidebar and top bar that renders one interface for a client and a different one for staff, from the same component. lib/guard.ts holds the server-side guards (requireUser, requireStaff, requirePermission) that every platform page and server action calls before doing anything. lib/permissions.ts is the authorization core beneath those guards: a role supplies default capabilities, and an account's own permissions JSON can override individual keys — every server action re-checks this, because a page rendering a control is never itself an authorization.

tour.title: The Data Layer
tour.description: lib/db/schema.ts is the entire Drizzle ORM schema in one file — Better Auth's own tables plus every business table (requests, quotes, invoices, subscriptions, demos, notifications). lib/db/index.ts wraps the Postgres pool in a Proxy so it is only constructed on first use, not at module load — necessary because CI builds the app with no DATABASE_URL at all. The site_content table is where Step 6's CMS overrides actually live: one jsonb row per editable homepage block, deep-merged over the code defaults on every read.
tour.languageLesson: Lazy initialization behind a Proxy defers the real work (opening a connection pool) until the first property access, letting a module be imported safely in environments — like a database-less CI build — where constructing it eagerly would fail.

tour.title: Platform Feature Areas: Billing, Demos, Realtime
tour.description: Three subsystems built on the authorization and data layers from Steps 8-9. BillingDocument.tsx renders a devis or facture as a styled PDF with @react-pdf/renderer, using money and company-identity values that can be overridden per document. lib/demos.ts models an owner-authored demo as an ordered list of typed blocks (link, credentials, upload, etc.) granted to named customers rather than a generic sandbox. lib/realtime.ts is the SSE backbone built on Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY that pushes live notifications, thread messages, and page refreshes to the browser whenever any of these subsystems write a change.
tour.languageLesson: Server-Sent Events over Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY: the payload is only a pointer (kind + entity id), never content, so the browser refetches the real data on each event — this keeps the realtime channel simple and avoids ever sending stale or oversized data down it.

tour.title: Containerization and CI/CD
tour.description: The Dockerfile is a multi-stage build for the production image: install dependencies with a frozen pnpm lockfile, build the Next.js app, then copy only the traced standalone output into a minimal Alpine runtime stage running as an unprivileged user. The GitHub Actions workflow verifies every push and pull request against main — lint, test, build — before a separate job publishes the image, gated on that verification passing and only running on pushes to main. Both stages ultimately run the scripts declared in package.json, closing the loop from source code back to a deployed container.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds use multiple FROM statements: a builder stage carries dev dependencies and compiles the app, while the final stage copies only the runtime artifacts across, keeping the shipped image small and free of build tooling.
